home.title: Calvimontes, S. C.
home.intro: Mechatronics Engineer (UPB, 2014; validated by EESC-USP, 2018), with a master's degree in Mechanical Engineering (PGMEC-UFF, 2018) and in Computational Modeling in Science and Technology (MCCT-UFF, 2024), plus ongoing complementary training in Computer Science (Estácio). His research line spans computational simulation of feedback control in multiphysics systems, with a background in welding-process modeling, computational homogenization, and multiscale simulation. He works as an independent researcher at the interfaces of engineering, computational modeling, control, and computing, with additional experience in automation, instrumentation, robotics, and electrical-electronic systems, and is also the founder of Editora Argus Kepheus, dedicated to multilingual technical literature.

items.title: ESP32 Asyncio Playground
items.description: Personal experiments with asynchronous processing (asyncio) on the ESP32 platform: LEDs, buttons, and multiple displays simulated in Wokwi.

detail.longDescription: Personal prototype to test the ESP32's asynchronous processing capabilities, starting from an original hands-on assessment (two LEDs, a button, and an OLED SSD1306 display) and experimentally extended: more LEDs, a second OLED, and a TFT ILI9341 display with live CPU and RAM usage graphs. The MicroPython firmware runs each task — LED blinking, button reading, display updates — as concurrent asyncio coroutines, with none blocking the others. Simulated on an ESP32-DevKitC V4 board in Wokwi.
detail.role: Development of the MicroPython firmware and the full circuit simulation in Wokwi, focused on validating asyncio concurrency patterns on the ESP32.
detail.results: Circuit validated with a progressive battery of tests (from the basic LED to full OLED diagnostics) and documented in a technical report and presentation. The thumbnail now reflects the extended version of the circuit, as simulated in Wokwi.

items.title: 2D Plotter
items.description: Control system for a two-axis Cartesian plotter for Arduino Uno, with joystick interface and OLED telemetry, simulated in Wokwi.

detail.longDescription: Control firmware for a two-axis Cartesian plotter: X/Y movement via A4988 drivers, pen height via servo motor, joystick interface, automatic homing, emergency stop, OLED display telemetry, speed bars, and relay-driven auxiliary loads. Travel limits are logical (no physical limit switches), designed for validation in simulation ahead of a future physical build.
detail.role: Development of the Arduino/C++ firmware, the circuit simulated in Wokwi, and the project's bilingual technical documentation.
detail.results: Validated with static consistency checks and documented in a LaTeX technical report.

items.title: Arduino Uno Cooperative
items.description: Native cooperative scheduler in C++ for Arduino Uno, no RTOS, controlling LEDs, buttons and two displays with timing and memory instrumentation, simulated in Wokwi.

detail.longDescription: Firmware exploring cooperative concurrency on an Arduino Uno R3/ATmega328P, without an RTOS, threads, or off-the-shelf scheduling libraries. A native, static cooperative scheduler runs eleven tasks: six independent blue LEDs sharing an adjustable interval, debounced scanning of three buttons, a diagnostic SSD1306 OLED, a primary ILI9341 TFT (over software SPI), and continuous instrumentation of CPU usage, free SRAM, lateness, and overruns. The project conceptually derives from esp32-asyncio, adapting the same idea of independent concurrent tasks to the ATmega328P's 8-bit, 2 KiB-SRAM constraints.
detail.role: Development of the Arduino/C++ firmware, the native cooperative scheduler, the circuit simulated in Wokwi, and the project's bilingual technical documentation.
detail.results: Validated with isolated diagnostic sketches for Wokwi and an acceptance checklist for the integrated build, documented in a LaTeX technical report.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.content: This policy summarizes the data flows implemented by this static website. It should be read together with the technical inventory in docs/PRIVACY_DATA_FLOW.md.

dataCollection.title: Data handled
dataCollection.content: The website avoids unnecessary collection. The main data involved is voluntarily submitted through the contact form and preferences stored locally in the browser.

personalData.title: Contact form
personalData.content: The site has two contact forms: submitting the message form sends name, email address, subject, message, and consent confirmation to the Formspree endpoint configured by the site; submitting the file form sends name, email address, message, a PDF attachment (up to 3 MB), a fixed subject label ("inbox-document", not user-editable), and consent confirmation to the Forminit endpoint configured by the site. The services may also process technical request metadata needed to deliver the message.

usage.title: Local preferences
usage.content: The website uses localStorage to remember the selected language and visual palette. These values remain in the user browser and can be removed by clearing site data.

lgpd.title: Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD)
lgpd.content: Where applicable, personal-data processing should follow the LGPD. This page describes the known data and keeps operational unknowns marked in the technical inventory until the external service account is reviewed.

controller.title: Controller
controller.content: The site owner decides the purpose of the contact form and receives submitted messages.

operator.title: Processor
operator.content: Formspree and Forminit act as the external services used to process and deliver contact-form messages (the message form and the file form, respectively). Each service's retention and deletion settings still need to be verified in the corresponding account.

cookies.title: Cookies and local storage
cookies.content: The first-party code of this website does not set cookies. Language and palette preferences are saved in localStorage, not cookies.

thirdParty.title: Third-party services
thirdParty.content: The site does not load Google Analytics, reCAPTCHA, advertising pixels, or embedded analytics. A request to Formspree occurs only when a valid form is submitted. External links are opened only when the user activates them.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.content: You may request access, correction, deletion, or clarification about personal data submitted through the form by using the public contact email shown on this site. Local preferences can also be deleted directly in the browser.

changes.title: Policy changes
changes.content: This policy may be updated when the website, contact form, or external services change. The date above shows the last recorded review.

contact.title: Contact
contact.content: For questions about this policy or about data submitted through the form, use the public email sergio.cordero.calvimontes@proton.me or the contact page on this site.
